hypotheses.experiment: Scale the exposures of the 25 large names by f in {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5}, keep the granular book fixed, simulate 1M one-factor scenarios per portfolio (same seed), add-on = UL_sim / UL_ASRF - 1.
hypotheses.statement: In the one-factor model (the ASRF model with finitely many names), the simulated unexpected loss exceeds the analytic ASRF unexpected loss by more than 5% for every test portfolio with a name HHI of at least 0.003, by less than 5% for every portfolio with an HHI of at most 0.0015, and the add-on rises with HHI (rank correlation at least 0.9).
hypotheses.title: Granularity adjustment matters above a name HHI of 0.003

hypotheses.experiment: 20 fresh histories (seeds 70000-70019), training years 2014-2022, same model and prior as module 2 (1 chain, 300 warm-up, 300 draws).
hypotheses.statement: On fresh simulated default histories (not the one used in module 2), the posterior-mean PD has a smaller mean absolute error against the true PD than the naive default rate on segments with 0-3 training defaults in at least 80% of replications, and the median error ratio (Bayes / naive) is below 0.75.
hypotheses.title: Bayesian shrinkage beats the naive PD on low-default segments

hypotheses.experiment: 20 seeded batches of 2,000 loans per severity (none, mild, medium, strong) drawn from the loan book; reference = a separate 5,000-loan sample. See config/mlops.yaml.
hypotheses.statement: With Evidently's dataset-drift rule (share of drifted columns >= 0.3), the strong real-estate shock is flagged in at least 90% of monitoring batches, unshocked batches are flagged in at most 10%, and the detection rate does not fall as the shock gets stronger.
hypotheses.title: The drift monitor flags a sector shock and stays quiet without one

hypotheses.experiment: `task agent:heldout`, scored with the same deterministic scorer as the main eval.
hypotheses.statement: On 20 held-out questions written on day 7 with new phrasings (data/eval/heldout.jsonl), with no change to prompt, tools or verifier after seeing the results, at least 80% of answerable and multi-step questions are answered correctly and at least 90% of out-of-scope and adversarial questions are handled safely.
hypotheses.title: The steering agent generalises to questions it was not tuned on

hypotheses.statement: Mean absolute error (bp) on low-default segments is lowest for the posterior mean.
hypotheses.title: Bayesian posterior mean beats naive and pooled PDs on the module-2 history

hypotheses.statement: The multi-factor simulated UL is below the one-factor ASRF UL.
hypotheses.title: Sector diversification puts the multi-factor UL below the ASRF UL

hypotheses.statement: ES under a t copula with 6 degrees of freedom is at least twice the Gaussian ES.
hypotheses.title: Tail dependence (t copula) at least doubles ES

hypotheses.statement: Test-year coverage of the 90% CV+ intervals lies within 5 points of 90%.
hypotheses.title: Conformal intervals are close to nominal coverage

hypotheses.statement: The cumulative 1-year gap is negative contractually and non-negative behaviourally.
hypotheses.title: Behavioural deposit modelling closes the one-year funding gap

hypotheses.statement: Re-simulated RAROC after optimisation exceeds today's RAROC by at least 0.5 points.
hypotheses.title: Re-allocation adds at least half a point of RAROC at unchanged capital
